_meta.note: Hands-off: everything in items[] is live (no pending state). sources[] are crawled weekly for events. The agent rewrites this each Thursday.

items.name: Sawyer Park
items.ages: all three, easy
items.note: Playground, paved paths for scooters, woods trail, real bathrooms. Right in town.

items.name: Memories Ice Cream
items.ages: crowd-pleaser
items.note: Iconic spot on an old dairy farm, huge portions. Great little add-on outing.

items.name: Exeter Bowling Lanes
items.ages: candlepin = light balls, good for 3yo
items.note: Candlepin bowling with small balls — actually doable for little hands. Cash only.

items.name: Swasey Parkway
items.ages: stroller-friendly
items.note: Riverside walk closed to cars; hosts the farmers market & town festivals.

items.name: Henderson-Swasey Town Forest
items.ages: easy trails, watch for bikes
items.note: Gentle wooded trails close to home. Bring a map — blazes can be faint.

items.name: Stillwells Riverwalk Ice Cream
items.ages: crowd-pleaser
items.note: Walk-up ice cream right on the Exeter riverwalk. Pairs with Swasey Parkway.

items.name: Imagine Art & Play
items.ages: perfect for 3 & 5
items.note: Imaginative-play rooms (vet, fire station, construction). Mornings only; closed Sun.

items.name: Captain's Cove Adventure Golf
items.ages: 7 & 5 love it, 3 tags along
items.note: Nautical-themed mini golf with a waterfall — and ice cream on site.

items.name: Hampton Beach
items.ages: all three
items.note: Classic sand beach with a boardwalk. Best on a warm, dry day.

items.name: Vernon Family Farm
items.ages: hay bales, animals, space to run
items.note: Beloved local farm with animals, a farm store, and frequent family events.

items.name: Mast Road Natural Area
items.ages: flat, accessible, bridges
items.note: Easy, mostly-accessible trails with boardwalks over the marsh. Good for little legs.

items.name: Seacoast Science Center
items.ages: touch tanks = magic for this age
items.note: Touch tanks, sea creatures, whale bones, plus an oceanfront state park. Closed Mon.

items.name: Hilltop Fun Center
items.ages: go-karts have a kid option
items.note: Mini golf, arcade, batting cages, laser tag, go-karts. Indoor + outdoor mix.

items.name: Charmingfare Farm
items.ages: pony & hayrides, hands-on
items.note: Hayrides, pony rides, feed the goats, see a camel & bear. Seasonal — check events.

items.name: XtremeCraze Londonderry
items.ages: huge inflatables for littles
items.note: Massive inflatable area, arcade, laser tag, pizza. Strong rainy-day option.

items.name: Fun City Trampoline Park
items.ages: toddler area for the 3yo
items.note: Big trampoline park with a separate little-kid zone. Burns a lot of energy.

items.name: Funspot
items.ages: all three, classic
items.note: The world's largest arcade — bowling, mini golf, hundreds of games. A real day trip.

items.name: Alnoba — Lewis Family Sculpture Park
items.ages: open trails + big outdoor sculptures to walk among
items.note: Outdoor sculpture park on wooded trails in Kensington — 30+ monumental works, room for the girls to roam. Often by appointment / event-based, so check hours before going.

items.name: Odiorne Point State Park
items.ages: Easy paths, rocky tidepools, a playground, and WWII bunkers — great for all three.
items.note: 135-acre oceanfront park in Rye with the Seacoast Science Center on-site, picnic areas, tidepooling. Day-use fee in season; watch the 3yo on the rocks.

items.name: Stratham Hill Park
items.ages: Two playgrounds (one toddler-sized), open fields, an easy fire-tower trail.
items.note: Town park with playgrounds, picnic pavilions, ballfields, and wooded trails to a fire tower. Free; grounds close during the summer 4-H Summerfest.

items.name: Henry Law Park & Splash Pad
items.ages: Adventure playground with a Gundalow boat, climbing tower, swings, plus a splash pad — perfect spread for 7/5/3.
items.note: Riverside Dover park beside the Children's Museum of NH. Splash pad runs warm months only; parking fills on hot weekend afternoons.

items.name: Wagon Hill Farm
items.ages: Short, mostly flat field trails down to a small bay beach; the iconic wagon and gentle hills suit little legs.
items.note: 40-acre Durham conservation farm on Little Bay with easy mowed-field paths and a tiny shore beach. Free; dogs off-leash dawn–10am.

items.name: Great Bay National Wildlife Refuge
items.ages: The Peverly Pond Trail is a flat, stroller-friendly 0.5-mi boardwalk loop — ideal for the youngest.
items.note: 1,000+ acre refuge on Newington's Great Bay shore with accessible boardwalk and wooded loops. Free; remote access road, minimal facilities.

items.name: Mount Agamenticus
items.ages: A short summit walk with a new universal-access path and 360° views; you can drive most of the way up.
items.note: 691-ft York summit with picnic tables and viewing platforms. Free; summit road/facilities seasonal, full loop is long for a 3yo.

items.name: Wells Reserve at Laudholm
items.ages: Easy field-and-forest trails lead to a quiet undeveloped beach; historic farm and salt marsh to look at.
items.note: Coastal estuarine reserve in Wells, 7 mi of easy trails + visitor center. Small fee Memorial Day–Oct, no pets, bring bug spray.

items.name: York Long Sands Beach
items.ages: Long, wide, flat sand with gentle surf and end tidepools — easy for the 3yo, room to roam for the older two.
items.note: ~1.5-mi sandy York beach with metered parking and nearby snack shops; calmer than Short Sands. Parking fills early, water stays cold.

items.name: Fuller Gardens
items.ages: Compact, stroller-easy estate rose gardens, a Japanese garden, and a small conservatory — a short, calm outing.
items.note: Turn-of-the-century estate rose garden in North Hampton, a block from the ocean. Paid admission, season ~spring–mid-Oct; best in bloom.

items.name: Prescott Park
items.ages: Free, flat, stroller-friendly riverside gardens with fountains and boats to watch on the Piscataqua.
items.note: Portsmouth's downtown waterfront park with flower gardens, fountains, and summer festivals; next to Strawbery Banke. Parking is tight.

items.name: Bedrock Gardens
items.ages: 30-acre whimsical garden with quirky metal sculptures and water features — a fun scavenger-hunt feel for the 5 & 7yo.
items.note: Nonprofit art-and-horticulture garden in Lee. Limited open days (Tue–Fri + 1st & 3rd weekends); paid admission — check the calendar first.

items.name: Maudslay State Park
items.ages: Gentle carriage-road paths past historic gardens, huge climbing trees, and meadows along the Merrimack.
items.note: Newburyport park, 16 mi of trails + historic gardens (mountain laurel peaks late May–June). $5 parking; side trails poorly marked.

items.name: Applecrest Farm Orchards
items.ages: Easy pick-your-own rows, hayrides, cider donuts and farm animals — all three can manage it.
items.note: NH's oldest/largest apple orchard; PYO apples, peaches, berries, pumpkins + farm store and creamery. PYO seasonal; fall weekends crowded.

items.name: Emery Farm
items.ages: Small, low-key petting area (goats, bunny, hens) plus a cafe — great for the 3 & 5yo.
items.note: One of the oldest family-run farms in the US (since 1660), with a market/cafe, PYO berries/pumpkins, and a small petting area. Animals seasonal.

items.name: Coppal House Farm
items.ages: Sunflower festival and corn maze are kid-pleasers; it's a working livestock farm, not a petting zoo.
items.note: 78-acre livestock/grain farm with a 6-acre corn maze and summer Sunflower Festival. Marquee events seasonal (sunflowers late Jul–Aug, maze Sept–Nov).

items.name: Legacy Lane Farm
items.ages: Donation-based petting zoo, close to home and very toddler-friendly for the 3yo.
items.note: Family-owned Stratham farm with a petting zoo plus farm camps and goat yoga. Limited days/hours (~Wed–Sun), donation admission — confirm hours.

items.name: DeMeritt Hill Farm
items.ages: Hayride to the orchard, two kids' play areas and gentle trails suit all three ages.
items.note: 120-acre PYO farm with play areas, hayrides, bakery. Heads-up: ownership change in early 2026 with a planned Aug-2026 reopen — verify it's open before going.

items.name: York's Wild Kingdom Zoo & Fun Park
items.ages: Zoo plus kiddie rides and deer/goat feeding — a big hit with the 5 & 7yo, manageable for the 3yo.
items.note: 25-acre privately owned zoo (lion, tiger, kangaroo, butterfly house) bundled with an amusement park. Seasonal (~Mem Day–Labor Day); can feel pricey.

items.name: Center for Wildlife
items.ages: Live raptors and resident animal ambassadors up close — calm, educational, good for curious kids.
items.note: Wildlife rehab center at the base of Mt. Agamenticus with a nature center and resident owls, hawks, turtles. Visitor hours limited — check schedule.

items.name: Explore the Ocean World Oceanarium
items.ages: Hands-on touch tanks with a biologist-led talk — engaging for all three; a solid rainy-day pick.
items.note: Small hands-on oceanarium at Hampton Beach with tanks of local Gulf of Maine creatures and a guided touch-tank tour. ~1 hr, seasonal — confirm hours.

items.name: Great Bay Discovery Center
items.ages: Estuarine touch tank, a play lobster boat and a flat boardwalk — excellent for the 3yo and the older two.
items.note: Free education center for the Great Bay Reserve with an indoor touch tank and a 1,700-ft accessible boardwalk. Indoor center seasonal (~May–Sept).

items.name: Ipswich River Wildlife Sanctuary
items.ages: Gentle trails where chickadees land on your hand; turtles, frogs and an observation tower keep kids engaged.
items.note: Mass Audubon's largest sanctuary (12+ mi of trails, observation tower), ~1 hr south. Closed Mondays; nominal admission. A walking/nature outing.

items.name: Joppa Flats Education Center
items.ages: Indoor exhibits and family drop-in programs, gateway to Plum Island wildlife — easy and short for younger kids.
items.note: Mass Audubon center at the gateway to Parker River NWR / Plum Island, with indoor exhibits and family programs. Hours limited (typically Tue–Sun).

items.name: Sky Zone Manchester
items.ages: Open jump for the 7 & 5; Toddler Time (Tue–Thu afternoons) gives the 3yo a calmer session.
items.note: Big trampoline park with dodgeball, foam pit, ninja course and a toddler area. Grip socks + waiver required. Farther option (~45 mi).

items.name: Off the Wall Kidz
items.ages: Sweet spot for all three: separate big-kid and toddler zones, so the 3yo has her own soft area.
items.note: All-day-play indoor playground with ball pits, slides and a small arcade (former Luv 2 Play space). Socks required; closes mid-afternoon weekdays.

items.name: Salt Pump Climbing Co. — Portsmouth
items.ages: Designated kids' area; bouldering (no ropes) suits the 7 & 5, the 3yo can scramble low traverses with a spot.
items.note: Bright bouldering-only gym (opened 2024) with a family kids' zone. Waiver required; opens noon weekdays, 10am weekends.

items.name: Seacoast Climb
items.ages: Kids' classes start at age 4 (target the 7 & 5); auto-belays let them top-rope. The 3yo: bouldering only.
items.note: Small gym with bouldering, top-rope, lead and auto-belays in Rye. Drop-in ~$20, open 7 days; waiver required.

items.name: Bowl-O-Rama Family Fun Center
items.ages: Great for all three — every lane has bumpers, candlepin's light balls are easy, big arcade for downtime.
items.note: 22 candlepin lanes with auto-scoring, a large arcade, and an on-site grill in Portsmouth. Weekend afternoons get busy — go early.

items.name: Rumors Sports Bar & Bowling
items.ages: Candlepin's small balls suit the 5 & 3yo; ask for bumpers. Better as a daytime pick with the girls.
items.note: Neighborhood candlepin alley with darts, billiards and a full bar in Newmarket. Leans adult in the evenings; call ahead for family open-bowl.

items.name: The Rinks at Exeter
items.ages: Closest rink to home. Public skate fits the 7 & 5; the 3yo can use a skating walker with a parent.
items.note: Two-rink complex with public skate, drop-ins and leagues. ~$15 + ~$5 rental; sessions vary daily — check the schedule first (~9 mi).

items.name: Dover Ice Arena
items.ages: Cheap, low-key public skate for all three — kids 3 and under free, so the 3yo skates at no cost.
items.note: City-run single-sheet arena with monthly public-skate schedules — call to confirm times. Note: closed for maintenance ~May 11–Jul 5, 2026.

items.name: Happy Wheels Skate Center
items.ages: Classic roller rink; the 7 & 5 will love it, toddler quad rentals mean the 3yo can wobble along too.
items.note: Beloved Greater-Portland roller rink with daily public sessions and cheap Family Nights. Farthest pick (~55 mi) — save for a day trip.

items.name: Children's Museum of New Hampshire
items.ages: Bullseye for 3/5/7 — hands-on exhibits (dino dig, submarine, music) skew toddler-to-age-10.
items.note: Two floors of interactive STEAM exhibits in downtown Dover. Timed-ticket sessions (AM/PM) and closed Mondays; reserve ahead on rainy weekends.

items.name: SEE Science Center
items.ages: 7 and 5 will love the hands-on physics; the 3yo can roam but some exhibits aim older.
items.note: 90+ hands-on exhibits plus the Guinness-record LEGO Millyard. ~45 mi in Manchester; small footprint, ~$9/person, weekend 10–5.

items.name: McAuliffe-Shepard Discovery Center
items.ages: Planetarium + space exhibits hit for 7 and 5; pick a short dome show for the 3yo.
items.note: NH's planetarium with a new dome system plus a hands-on science floor (~50 mi, Concord). Shows run on a schedule and sell out; closed Mon/Tue.

items.name: Wonder Mountain Fun Park
items.ages: 7 and 5 can putt and ride; the 3yo needs an adult on the kart and may be too small to drive solo.
items.note: Two themed mini-golf courses, a go-kart track, NE's largest man-made maze, and a 45-game arcade (~25 mi, Wells ME). Seasonal; kart height min.

items.name: Fun-O-Rama Arcade
items.ages: Nostalgic, easy wins for all three — many games still 25¢, plus bumper cars and small rides for the 3yo.
items.note: 10,000 sq ft vintage arcade on Short Sands Beach with 250+ games, bumper cars, mini-golf (~22 mi, York ME). Seasonal (Mem Day–Columbus Day).

items.name: Krazy Kids Indoor Play & Party Center
items.ages: Four-story climbing structure plus a toddler 'Tot Spot' — genuinely covers 3, 5 and 7 at once.
items.note: Four-story indoor playground with climbing structure, bungee tower, ropes course, trampolines and an arcade (~47 mi, Pembroke). 2-hr admission; socks required.

items.name: Discovery Museum
items.ages: Purpose-built for this age band — separate younger and older zones plus an outdoor treehouse.
items.note: Hands-on science/nature museum on a 4.5-acre campus with an accessible Discovery Woods treehouse (~50 mi, Acton MA — far edge). Timed tickets advised.

items.name: Hampstead Stage Company
items.ages: Interactive book-based shows with quick costume changes — engaging for 5 and 7; the 3yo may fidget.
items.note: Touring two-actor children's theater adapting classic books, performing at libraries/venues around NH. No fixed venue — check the calendar for a nearby date.

items.name: Lago's Ice Cream
items.ages: Easy, beloved stop for all three — homemade flavors, outdoor seating, near the coast.
items.note: Family-run homemade ice cream for 40+ years on Rte 1 in Rye, a classic Seacoast stand (~15 mi). Seasonal hours, walk-up window, weekend lines.

items.name: Annabelle's Natural Ice Cream
items.ages: 40+ flavors and a waterfront stroll afterward — a true outing for all three, not just a quick cone.
items.note: Portsmouth icon since 1982 steps from the working waterfront — grab a cone and walk to the water (~18 mi). Tiny shop, street parking only.

items.name: Guinea Pig Sanctuary
items.ages: Interactive setting with gentle guinea pigs; all three ages welcome
items.note: Licensed non-profit rescue sanctuary in Salisbury, MA (~45 mi) with family play days and guided tours. Free admission, no appointments needed. Offers ESGP program for children with special needs.

items.name: Hampton Falls Farmers Market
items.ages: Great for all ages 3–7
items.note: Seasonal farmers market in the Seacoast area with fresh local produce, crafts, and family-friendly browsing. Check the market calendar for exact dates and times.

items.name: Amesbury Town Park
items.note: Big municipal park with playground, splash pad (seasonal), skate park, and open fields. Free entry; parking can be tight on busy days.

items.name: Stone Zoo
items.ages: Snow leopard, red pandas, reindeer, black bears, splash pad and playground — engaging for all three.
items.note: 26-acre Zoo New England property in Stoneham, MA (~50 mi). Walk-up tickets available; Sat–Sun 9am–6pm. Carousel runs weekends only. EBT/WIC families: $5/person.

items.name: O'Neil Cinemas Brickyard Square — Epping
items.ages: All three — walk-up tickets, monthly sensory-friendly screenings at 10am for kids with sensory sensitivities
items.note: 12-screen multiplex at Brickyard Square in Epping (~13 mi). Walk-up tickets, family films most weekends. Monthly sensory-friendly screenings at 10am on select dates — check schedule.

items.name: Parlee Farms
items.ages: PYO rows at a relaxed pace — great for all three; littlest ones love plucking berries.
items.note: 100-acre PYO farm in Tyngsboro MA (~40 mi): strawberries June, cherries June–July, blueberries July–Aug, peaches Aug, apples/pumpkins fall. Open Tue–Sun 10–5 (Sat 10–4). Check Today's Farm News on the website before going for picking availability.

items.name: Cider Hill Farm
items.ages: Easy PYO rows the 3yo can work alongside the older two; barnyard animals and a cafe on-site.
items.note: 145-acre PYO farm in Amesbury MA (~12 mi): strawberries, raspberries, blueberries in summer; apples (50+ varieties) Aug–Oct. Farm store and barnyard open daily 8am–6pm. PYO tickets available walk-up or online.

items.name: Exeter Farmers Market
items.ages: easy, free
items.note: Every Thursday 2:30–6 PM (closes 5:30 after Oct 1), May–October at Swasey Parkway. Local produce, food trucks, often live music.

items.name: NH SPCA Story Time with the Animals
items.ages: ages 2–5, perfect for the 3yo
items.note: Read a story then meet shelter animals at the NH SPCA humane education room in Stratham (~6 mi). Tuesdays & Thursdays at 10:45 AM all summer. Free; registration recommended.

items.name: Seacoast Science Center — Sensory Friendly Hour
items.ages: all ages; especially helpful for kids with sensory sensitivities
items.note: Every Sunday 9–10 AM before general public opens — quieter, calmer access to touch tanks and exhibits. Regular SSC admission applies.

items.name: Hampton Beach Sea Shell Stage — Free Summer Concerts
items.ages: free outdoor boardwalk stage, all ages
items.note: Free nightly concerts at the Sea Shell Stage 7–9:30 PM all summer long. Two sets nightly — pair with a beach walk and boardwalk ice cream.

items.name: Rodgers + Hammerstein's Cinderella — Prescott Park
items.ages: fairy-tale classic — great for the 5 & 7yo, the 3yo will love the songs and costumes
items.note: 2026 Prescott Park signature musical: R+H Cinderella on the waterfront stage in Portsmouth. Thu–Sun at 7 PM June 19–Aug 9; matinees July 5 & July 25 at 1 PM. ASL shows June 28, July 9, July 18, July 25. Bring a blanket/chairs. $20 suggested donation — no one turned away.

items.name: Toy Story 5 — O'Neil Cinemas Epping
items.ages: Pixar classic characters — great for all three
items.note: Toy Story 5 opens June 19 — Woody, Buzz and the gang vs. a tablet. Playing at O'Neil Cinemas Brickyard Square in Epping (~13 mi). Check showtimes at epping.oneilcinemas.com; sensory-friendly screenings available on select dates at 10am.

items.name: Josie's Family Jams — Prescott Park
items.ages: free kids' outdoor music series — ideal for the 3–7 crowd
items.note: Free outdoor family music series at Prescott Park waterfront, Sundays at 4 PM through early August. Live music and dancing for kids — bring a blanket. Pairs beautifully with an Annabelle's ice cream run afterward.

items.name: Stratham 4-H Summerfest
items.ages: antique tractors, fire vs. police softball, helicopters, food — fun for all three
items.note: Free family festival at Stratham Hill Park replacing the cancelled Stratham Fair. Fri July 17, 2–9 PM; Sat July 18, 8 AM–2 PM (main day for families); Sun July 19, 10–11 AM (closing). 4-H clubs, antique tractor show, fire vs. police softball, helicopter & fire truck demos, food. Right next door to Kensington.

items.name: Camp ENCORE! Willy Wonka KIDS — Prescott Park
items.ages: Willy Wonka performed by young campers — imaginative and fun for 3–10yo
items.note: Camp ENCORE! youth production of Willy Wonka KIDS at Prescott Park waterfront stage. Sat July 18 at 11 AM and 1 PM (two shows); Sun July 19 at 11 AM and 1 PM. Free/suggested donation — no one turned away. Bring a blanket or low beach chairs.

items.name: Native American Pow-Wow — Wells, ME
items.ages: drumming, dancing, crafts, food — vivid and engaging for all three ages
items.note: 22nd annual pow-wow hosted by NH Intertribal Native American Council at Wells Harbor Park, 331 Harbor Rd, Wells ME. Sat July 18, 10am–5pm; Sun July 19, 10am–4pm. Traditional drumming, regalia dancing, artisan vendors, food, and cultural demos. Walk-up admission. ~45 mi north.

items.name: Cider Hill Farm — Blueberry & Flower Festival
items.ages: PYO blueberries + flowers, barnyard animals — all three ages love this
items.note: Cider Hill Farm's summer pick-your-own celebration across two weekends (July 18–19 and 25–26). U-pick blueberries and flowers, farm activities, barnyard animals, and the farm store/cafe. Walk-up tickets on-site. ~12 mi south in Amesbury MA.

items.name: Teddy Bear Clinic & Picnic — Rochester
items.ages: toddlers and young kids — bring a favorite stuffed animal for a pretend check-up
items.note: Free community event in Central Square Rochester, Saturday July 18, 10am–noon. Kids bring a stuffed animal or teddy bear for a pretend 'check-up' with medical volunteers — a sweet, low-key way to demystify doctor visits. Free; ~22 mi north of Kensington.

items.name: Summer in the Street — Portsmouth
items.ages: free outdoor street music, all ages — stroller-friendly closed road
items.note: Free Saturday evening concert series on Pleasant Street in downtown Portsmouth, 5:30–8:30 PM (road closed 4–9 PM). July 18: The Shanty Crew (PMAF Maritime Folk); July 25: T.J. Wheeler & Hatrack Gallagher; Aug 1: Seacoast Wind Ensemble. BYOC; food and drink nearby. No alcohol on the street.

items.name: Coppal House Farm — Sunflower Festival
items.ages: walk-through sunflowers, live music, farm activities — great for all three
items.note: Annual sunflower festival at Coppal House Farm, 118 N River Rd, Lee NH. Open daily 10am–6pm while sunflowers are in bloom. Live music, artisan craft vendors, local food, and acres of walking paths through oilseed sunflowers. Walk-up tickets at the gate (discounted online at nhsunflower.com). ~15 mi from Kensington.

items.name: Yankee Homecoming — Newburyport, MA
items.ages: parades, waterfront concerts, craft fair, Family Day, fireworks — all ages
items.note: Newburyport's 69th annual 9-day festival (July 25–Aug 2). Theme: Home Sweet Home. Waterfront concerts, Grand Parade, juried art & craft fair, Family Day, U.S. Coast Guard Open House, and a fireworks finale. Most events free and walk-up. ~25 mi south in Newburyport MA.

items.name: Custom House Lawn Concerts — Newburyport
items.ages: free outdoor music by the Merrimack River, all ages
items.note: Summer Sunday concert series on the lawn at the Custom House Maritime Museum, 25 Water St, Newburyport — steps from the waterfront. 4–6 PM, walk-up, free or suggested donation. Bring chairs or a blanket. Check for weekly lineup. ~25 mi south.

items.name: Portsmouth Farmers Market
items.ages: easy, free, great for all ages
items.note: Saturday morning market at 1 Junkins Ave (near the waterfront), Portsmouth. 8 AM–12 PM. Local produce, bread, flowers, cheese, prepared foods. Pair with a Prescott Park walk or Annabelle's ice cream. Free to browse.

items.name: Ellis Park Free Beach Concerts — York, ME
items.ages: beach + free live music — all ages, classic summer evening
items.note: Free nightly concerts at Ellis Park right on Short Sands Beach, York ME. Evening shows, walk-up, donations welcome. Genres rotate — folk, jazz, blues, brass. Pair with Short Sands swimming and nearby Fun-O-Rama arcade or ice cream. ~22 mi north. Check yorkparksandrec.org for the weekly lineup.

items.name: Camp ENCORE! Mean Girls JR. — Prescott Park
items.ages: youth campers performing Mean Girls JR. — fun for school-age kids and their families
items.note: Camp ENCORE! teen musical theatre intensive culminating in Mean Girls JR. at Prescott Park waterfront stage. Sat Aug 1 at 1 PM and Sun Aug 2 at 1 PM. Free/suggested donation — no one turned away. Bring a blanket or low beach chairs.

items.name: Vernon Family Farm — Fried Chicken Night (August)
items.ages: family-friendly outdoor farm dinner, open grounds with animals
items.note: Monthly 2nd-Saturday farm dinner: fried chicken, local food vendors, live music 5–7:30 PM. Grounds open 4–8 PM; food is paid.

sources.name: Crowned Hawk Classic 5K and One Mile
O'Neil Cinemas Epping — sensory-friendly & current films
